stable.body:
# Changelog

## Unreleased

## 0.2.2-Stable - 2026-11-09

### Lite

- Publish a Zygisk-free Lite ZIP with the Tricky Store manager, RKP workbench and
  device RKP issuer. Full remains the default update edition.
- Publish independent SPDX inventories, build-provenance and SBOM attestations
  for both editions in the same release.

### Device Faker

- Add per-app device profiles, reusable templates and installed app selection. Resolve
  profiles and target assignments separately for each Android user.
- Embed 207 searchable device presets contributed by SkyQiQiQwQ in Issue #48.
  Preserve supplied identity, marketing and build fields without filling missing values.
  Review and edit presets before adding them to a draft; saving and enabling remain separate.
- Add brand filtering, fingerprint mismatch notices and accessible field review across
  all 16 locales, including narrow layouts and right-to-left text.

### Play Integrity

- Add Full injection mode and expose process-level activation diagnostics in the WebUI.
- Default the engine to disabled unless explicitly enabled. Keep existing explicit
  enable settings and leave configuration import, preview and application independent
  of the power setting.

### Remote Key Provisioning

- Allow users to include a build fingerprint explicitly in remote signing requests.
- Recognize `rkpdapp.google.apk` in the system RKP APEX for device V1 provisioning.

### Language spoofing

- Add per-app and per-user language rules in the Full edition through Zygisk.

### ZRAM

- Add swap inventory, runtime ZRAM configuration and opt-in boot profiles. Protect
  devices managed by the system and preserve saved settings across failed changes.

### Linux environments

- Reject ARM64 core dumps, malformed load segments and unavailable ELF interpreters
  during import; resolve interpreter paths within the guest filesystem.
- Distinguish zombie processes from live guests and reject symbolic links used as
  private state directories.
- Preserve edited drafts across external configuration changes, identify invalid fields
  and distinguish empty logs from missing environments across all 16 locales.

- Preserve cancellation codes during decompression, handle concurrent cgroup removal,
  and verify the final init identity and supervisor lease before confirming stop.
- Drain final log output, refresh active runtime state without filling operation history,
  and make inspection feedback, cancelled imports and disabled settings explicit.

- Import trusted ARM64 rootfs archives with inspected SHA-256 verification, bounded
  extraction, asynchronous progress, cancellation and private staging.
- Manage private mounts, terminal entry, foreground services, DNS, bounded logs and
  optional startup after boot. Use PID namespaces or cgroup v2 to track guest processes.
- Confirm changes against the current configuration revision and preserve data when
  termination cannot be verified. Keep all 16 locales and RTL layouts aligned with
  existing interface components.

### Kernel modules

- Reject duplicate or unreadable ELF metadata sections, and mark inferred or repeated
  module names explicitly during inspection.
- Validate load parameters by UTF-8 bytes before confirmation, with localized field errors
  and persistent inspection progress/error feedback across 16 locales.
- Protect the `kernelsu` root core from unloading, reject unknown holder state, and
  expose protection reasons consistently in the backend and all 16 interface locales.
- Use explicit confirmation action labels and isolate module names in RTL sentences;
  preserve confirmation content through close transitions and label module taint accurately.
- Add a separate Linux kernel module browser with loaded/sysfs-only state, references,
  dependents, runtime metadata and read-only parameters.
- Browse standard Android module directories and inspect uncompressed `.ko` ELF metadata.
- Add confirmed, serialized runtime load/unload operations with inspected-file digest checks,
  dependency checks, kernel-enforced restrictions and explicit unknown-outcome timeout reports.
- Match Android kernel procfs variants and keep release-prefix comparison advisory for
  symbol-versioned modules. Check ELF class/byte order and preserve parameter whitespace.
- Validate worker protocol/results, bound process cleanup, and retain partial read failures.
- Add localized runtime states, isolated technical strings, persistent operation feedback,
  keyboard focus restoration and layouts that adapt to larger text across 16 locales.

## 0.2.1-Stable - 2026-10-26

### Play Integrity

- Fetch selectable Pixel release fingerprints from Google build metadata, with
  Pixel 6a selected by default. Preview candidates and save their source metadata
  without applying them or enabling the engine. Leave unknown patch dates unset.
- Add quick controls for Build, property and Play Store fingerprint overrides.
  Explain the Play Store SDK compatibility mode and its precedence over fingerprints.
- Preview system, vendor and boot patch policies separately while retaining
  unselected partition settings and backend-specific formats.
- Persist process restart and device reboot requirements across page reloads.
  Keep independent keystore recovery available when an activation marker fails.
- Compare process-local Build and property snapshots with the saved configuration,
  matching revision, boot identity, PID and process start time. Import decoded
  integrity reports as unverified summaries; missing labels remain unknown.
- Extend configuration, recovery, JNI and mobile browser regression coverage,
  including narrow English, Chinese and right-to-left layouts. Local diagnostics
  and tests do not establish a Google Play Integrity verdict.

### Translations

- Add Ukrainian and Polish translations and localize the new integrity controls.

## 0.2.0-Stable - 2026-10-24

### Integrity and keystore compatibility

- Keep OEM lock-state and AVB property changes in their appropriate boot stages,
  including when Play Integrity is disabled, unconfigured or falls back after a failure.
- Validate SHA-256/SHA-512 boot hashes against backend requirements before saving.
  Preserve independent OhMyKeymint trust settings when only the prop handler changes.
- Serialize keystore configuration writes, restore failed updates, retain unknown
  default and per-app policy fields, and reject stale configuration or backend selections.
- Keep unsaved property and policy edits across background refreshes. Add explicit
  property reload and report settings that require a reboot.
- Align module disable/remove handling across the CLI, shell and native companion.
  Reject invalid compatibility options consistently without changing saved enable intent.
- Respect separate system, vendor and boot patch values when preparing optional
  keystore synchronization. Retain explicit configurations and skip incompatible
  single-date updates.

### Device provisioning

- Add MediaTek SoC detection, AIDL V1 RKP support and TrustKernel device-ID
  provisioning while retaining Qualcomm-specific defaults and backend selection.
- Refuse contradictory platform evidence and retain diagnostics for failed native
  provisioning. Firmware support and successful hardware issuance remain device-specific.

### Verification

- Extend configuration rollback, lifecycle, native/JVM, contract and mobile WebUI
  regression coverage, including API 36 AVD checks with KernelSU 3.3.0 and
  OhMyKeymint 1.2.0-b12557c.
- Local tests and emulator behavior do not establish Google Play Integrity verdicts
  or physical-device TEE, fingerprint and display compatibility.

## 0.1.8-stable - 2026-10-24

### Play Integrity

- Integrate a separately built Play Integrity Fork-derived engine with an opt-in
  configuration workflow, generation of Pixel Canary candidates, compatibility
  controls, diagnostics and history. Candidate generation and local configuration
  do not guarantee any Google Play Integrity verdict.
- Preview changes before applying configuration or optional keystore patch policies.
  Support structured field editing, raw import/export, saved profiles, migration,
  rollback, and confirmation before recovering an interrupted update.
- Make engine activation and emergency disable independent from configuration reads,
  including during errors and pending cleanup. Restore managed state when disabling.
- Improve phone-sized layouts: consistent navigation, panels, editor controls and
  preview alignment. Preserve drafts while switching tabs and correct Back behavior.

### Reliability and updates

- Paginate command history and diagnose empty backend responses.
- Handle different fingerprint-generator output paths and improve its diagnostics.
- Fall back to an English release download link when a Telegram ZIP exceeds the
  Bot API's upload limit.

### Licensing and verification

- Keep the derived engine under GPLv3 with upstream notices, and retain the
  independently implemented management interface under MIT.
- Link to the immutable build commit for corresponding source rather than
  embedding a duplicate source archive in the module.
- Add independent engine compilation, packaging checks, contract tests and
  mobile WebUI regression coverage to CI.

## 0.1.7-stable - 2026-10-19

### Tricky Store manager

- Accept EC-only keyboxes for OhMyKeymint while retaining certificate-chain and
  certificate-count validation for every supplied key.
- Preserve legacy and modern Xposed module detection with zip 9 through exact
  central-directory path lookups, including APKs with non-UTF-8 filenames.

### Dependencies

- Upgrade zip to 9.0.4 and refresh Rust and WebUI dependencies and lockfiles.

## 0.1.6-stable - 2026-10-18

### WebUI

- Run shell commands through the host's queued job API when available, so slow
  commands no longer block return navigation. Preserve output, exit status and
  compatibility with hosts that only provide `exec`.
- Stop restarting failed automatic update checks on each return to the home page;
  keep manual retries and channel changes available. Read the fixed hosting module
  identity once per WebUI session.
- Reduce target-list reconstruction overhead with shallow query snapshots, stable
  drafts and lightweight selection indicators. Measure new virtual rows through
  ResizeObserver to avoid repeated forced layout, including with enlarged text.
- Clean up command callbacks on completion and launch failures, including hosts
  that report a companion error after a nonzero exit.

## 0.1.5-stable - 2026-10-18

### WebUI

- Virtualize target and system-app lists while preserving search, bulk selection,
  keyboard focus and per-app controls. Batch synchronous package metadata lookups
  and stop queued lookups when their query is cancelled.
- Preserve edits made during target saves, update the saved baseline without an
  extra package-manager query, and guard overlapping writes.
- Keep RKP navigation available during loading, prevent overlapping profile
  operations, and discard results for changed inputs.
- Fix cached Device ID form initialization, language-switch races, cancelled file
  reads and malformed repository messages. Bound uploads and translation requests.
- Adapt buttons, tabs, forms, menus, dialogs and sheets to narrow screens, landscape
  and enlarged text. Wrap technical values and application names, improve supporting
  text size and contrast, and respect display safe areas.

## 0.1.4-stable - 2026-10-17

### RKP Workbench

- Add **Import DICE materials** as the main workbench entry, with separate offline
  validation, diagnostic CSR construction and online issuance commands. An existing CSR
  is not required; device collection and firmware patching are not implemented here.
- Preserve the imported chain, match explicit signing material to its leaf key, and
  construct a new CSR v3 using a fresh server challenge and newly generated attestation key.
- Share issuance and export between imported material and the labelled experimental
  degenerate-chain mode. Remove implicit offline fallback and successful error results.
- Select returned chains by public key, verify certificate signatures and constraints,
  and publish private keyboxes atomically after XML readback checks. JSON results contain
  paths and summaries instead of private XML. Installation remains independent.
- Bump the workbench feature contract to 2. Old profiles retain their seed derivation;
  material import does not overwrite profiles or an installed keybox.
- Accepts the integer DICE mode allowed by the `android.14` profile.
- Verification uses generated synthetic keys and a local simulated server. Real-material
  production acceptance and successful production export remain unverified for this path.

### Device RKP Issuer
- Automatic mode tries V2, AIDL V1 and native V1 in order, skipping unavailable methods.
  Any issuance or validation failure advances to the next method with a fresh challenge;
  failures are aggregated only after every method fails. Successful results include an
  attempt history. Local file writes happen after certificate validation succeeds.
- Adds the `v1-native` backend for vendor command `0x311e`. Native V1 reuses the
  V1 CSR assembler, structural checks and isolated worker, and does not require a system
  AIDL APK at runtime. Firmware and server acceptance remain unverified.
- Reports protocol and backend separately, exposes native V1 resource availability,
  and uses feature contract 5 across the CLI and WebUI.
- Adds the V1 AIDL signing oracle for Qualcomm PureSoft firmware with a zero HBK,
  adapted from LazyBonesLZY/rkp-v1-oracle under its MIT license.
- Adds automatic and explicit V1/V2 protocol selection.
- Selects the full EEK chain for the HAL's reported curve and uses the device's AIDL
  proxy in an isolated process, with bounded exchange files and timeout cleanup.
- Reports V1 as structurally checked; encrypted signing evidence is verified by the
  provisioning server. V2 retains local signature verification.
- Cross-checks Qualcomm aliases (including QTI/QCOM), SoC part numbers, hardware properties
  and kernel SoC information. Unknown and conflicting evidence have separate blockers;
  empty properties no longer imply support. The WebUI shows the evidence and keeps firmware
  and server compatibility unverified.
- Recognizes QTI as Qualcomm and gives the isolated worker vendor library search paths,
  retaining the default namespace's system dependency links for libraries such as libcrypto.
- Preserves worker error types and accepts bare as well as field-61-wrapped CSRs.
- Bounds exchange-file reads, rejects nonregular files and symlinks, and requires exactly
  one nonempty certificate chain for the requested key.
- Reserves private output directories atomically, removes partial runs on write failure,
  and saves keyboxes and private keys with mode `0600`, including explicit output copies.
- Uses the prerequisite report's device fingerprint consistently; an explicit fingerprint
  can satisfy a missing fingerprint without bypassing other prerequisites.
- Corrects the key export description: the exported keybox includes a software-generated
  private key; this path does not extract a private key from the TEE.

### TEE Attestation Extractor
- New offline tool for extracting Keybox XML and PEM material from existing captures and
  verifying private-key correspondence, certificate signatures and chain completeness.
- Verifies candidate RKP identity material against the signing leaf of a locally verified
  CSR, with separate Ed25519-seed, P-256-seed and P-256-scalar modes and raw capture offsets.
- Returns summaries without exposing private material. Explicit exports use private output
  directories and owner-only files; mismatched identity material cannot be exported.
- Adds binary uploads, device file paths, manager installation through an extension point,
  and translations in all 14 languages. Device-side acquisition is not included.
- Local checks do not establish root trust, revocation status, registration or server acceptance.
  Supported private keys are EC P-256/P-384 and RSA 2048–8192; RSA-1024 is unsupported.
- Verifies private-key PEM labels against their DER encoding. Inline inputs are limited
  to 32 KiB per file to fit shell transport; device file paths accept up to 256 KiB.
- Finds XML document boundaries through parsed tags, accepts closing-tag whitespace,
  and rejects illegal XML characters before exporting material.
- Rejects trailing data in CSR CBOR items, including embedded signed payloads, protected
  headers, DICE subject keys and configuration descriptors.
- Resolves same-name certificate issuers by signature and handles self-issued key rotation
  certificates without treating them as self-signed roots.
- Ignores root-tag examples in XML comments outside the captured document.

### WebUI
- Keeps long error details, links and code within the viewport.

### Command wrapper
- Preserves backend failure exit codes and tries fallback binaries only after execution
  failures (`126` or `127`).

## 0.1.3-stable - 2026-10-17

### Device RKP Issuer
- New tool: signs a P-256 key we generated with this device's Qualcomm KeyMint TA
  (`CSR_V2`, command `0x3122` over `libkeymasterdeviceutils.so`) and submits the resulting
  `AuthenticatedRequest` to Google's RKP server, then exports `keybox.xml` plus its private
  key. The request does not extract a private key from the TEE.
- Warns twice before it can run, and the backend refuses a run without
  `--acknowledge-limitations`: only some devices work, and only RKP certificates can be
  issued.
- Checks Android arm64, root, `/dev/smcinvoke`, `libkeymasterdeviceutils.so` and a Qualcomm
  SoC first, and reports exactly which prerequisite is missing.
- Validates the device's CSR (DICE chain, signature, challenge, `keysToSign`) and binds the
  issued certificate chain to the generated key before writing anything. The chain must also
  be one leaf-to-root path with no certificate left off it. These local shape and key
  checks do not establish certificate trust, revocation status or server acceptance.

## 0.1.2-stable - 2026-10-11

### Tricky Store manager
- Complete port of Tricky Addon (Update Target List):
  - Target list with modes, per-app policy, search, bulk selection, DenyList, unnecessary
    apps, system apps and auto-add.
  - Keyboxes from AOSP, "unknown", a local file, the keybox repository and custom providers,
    with import and export.
  - Prop settings, default policy with *Today*, help, keyboard shortcuts and its 23
    translations, including right-to-left languages.
- One manager for Tricky Store (`config.ini` and legacy `target.txt`), TEESimulator
  (`config.json`) and OhMyKeymint (`config.toml` + `injector.toml`).
  - The validation rules follow each module's own sources.
  - Unknown sections, comments and keys are preserved.
- Optional WebUI entry on the keystore module (plus the action button on Magisk), and the
  TSupport-Advance auto-target stop flag.
- Tricky Addon's in-app translation update, translation guide and Telegram link.
- Checked against the real modules on a KernelSU device, which found and fixed:
  - OhMyKeymint v1.2.0 rejected our `injector.toml` (an unknown `version` key) while the
    WebUI reported success. `[scoop.<package>]` tables are now read and written like
    OhMyKeymint's own parser does.
  - The "unknown" keybox now gives each key a two-certificate chain. Tricky Addon's
    single-certificate keybox only loads on Tricky Store: TEESimulator and OhMyKeymint
    refuse it.
  - TEESimulator accepts EC-only keyboxes, such as the RKP workbench exports.
  - Saving tells when OhMyKeymint needs a restart to apply a change.

### WebUI
- Rebuilt on Vue 3.5, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS 4 and shadcn-vue.
  - A black and white theme, light or dark, where color only marks errors, success and
    warnings.
  - Designed for phones along Material 3 Expressive:
    - 48dp touch targets and a visible response to every press.
    - Round buttons that square up while pressed, segmented lists, and spring motion.
    - A large title that collapses into the 64dp app bar, for one-handed reach.
    - Tonal gray surfaces instead of borders and shadows, with contrast checked
      against WCAG.
  - Menus, tabs and button groups mirror in right-to-left languages too.
  - Follows the KernelSU manager's window insets.
  - The Android back gesture closes dialogs and sheets.
- Every tool in 14 languages: English, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean,
  Spanish, French, German, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Arabic, Vietnamese and
  Indonesian.
- Help: long links and code wrap inside the page, and two slips in upstream translations
  (a link missing its parenthesis, a code span closed with a quote) no longer show raw
  Markdown.
- Every tool is a self-contained feature folder, discovered automatically.
  - Features plug into each other only through extension points.
  - Every backend response is validated against a schema.
- A tool whose backend feature is missing or on another contract version is disabled
  instead of misreading data.
- Unit tests (Vitest) and end-to-end tests (Playwright against a mock KernelSU host) with
  light, dark, right-to-left and Chinese screenshots.
- Contract tests run every API call through `duckctl.sh` and a real `duckd` build and
  parse the results with the WebUI's schemas.
- Device tests (`scripts/device-test.sh`) drive the WebUI inside the real KernelSU manager
  with each keystore module installed.
- Loads as seven files instead of about eighty. The KernelSU manager reads each request
  through a root shell, so this halved the load time on a slow device.
- Type-checked on the TypeScript 7 engine through typescript-native-bridge.

### Backend
- `duckd` builds its CLI from a feature registry. `duckd features` reports the compiled-in
  features, and each feature can be built alone.
- New `system` feature: module and device summary, stable and canary updates with changelog,
  output files, command history, uninstall and reboot.
- RKP profiles read their device defaults from AOSP build properties.
- Updated RustCrypto to its current generation (p256/p384 0.14, ed25519/x25519 3, aes-gcm
  0.11, x509-cert 0.3). Keys derived from saved seeds are pinned by regression tests.

### Module
- Scripts follow the KernelSU module guide:
  - Late-load support (`late-load.sh`).
  - A late prop pass after boot for values the system sets late.
  - The module description goes into KernelSU's temporary config.
- Magisk runs the boot-completed work from `service.sh`.
- The prop handler adds `ro.boot.vbmeta.size`, and applies the boot hash even when the
  handler is disabled, as upstream does.
- Uninstalling removes entry links, flags and saved data.

### Tooling
- CI fails when any source file in any language exceeds 600 lines.
- CI: NDK r30, Node 24, pnpm 12, WebUI lint/format/unit/E2E, per-feature builds.
- Canary artifacts are the installable module directory.
- Dependabot opens one pull request per major update.

CI run: https://github.com/eltavine/Duck-ToolBox/actions/runs/42574248406

GPLv3 device-faker corresponding source: https://github.com/eltavine/Duck-ToolBox/tree/f0626bd6f327a783a5f74420876050775d0324ed/components/device-faker

GPLv3 play-integrity corresponding source: https://github.com/eltavine/Duck-ToolBox/tree/f0626bd6f327a783a5f74420876050775d0324ed/components/play-integrity

- Full (default update): `duck-toolbox-0.2.2-Stable.zip`
- Lite (manual installation and updates): `duck-lite-0.2.2-Stable.zip`

Lite includes the Tricky Store manager, RKP workbench and device RKP issuer. It uses a separate module ID. Uninstall the other edition and reboot before switching.

Each installable ZIP has build-provenance and SPDX 2.3 SBOM attestations. The SBOM inventories delivered files and pinned source/build inputs; it is not a measured binary dependency graph.

Verify the downloaded ZIP with GitHub CLI:

```sh
gh attestation verify 'duck-toolbox-0.2.2-Stable.zip' --repo eltavine/Duck-ToolBox --signer-workflow eltavine/Duck-ToolBox/.github/workflows/ci.yml --source-digest f0626bd6f327a783a5f74420876050775d0324ed --source-ref refs/heads/main --deny-self-hosted-runners
```

For the SBOM attestation, add `--predicate-type https://spdx.dev/Document/v2.3`. Substitute the Lite filename to verify Lite. The matching Sigstore bundles can also be supplied with `--bundle`.

## v2.3 —— 夜间模式改成「绝对判据 + 周期复查」（versionCode 5）

修一个会让「日落到日出」整晚不生效的判定缺陷。

- **根因**：v2.1 的守护拿「重启前那一刻的昼夜判定」当基准，重启前若已经是错的，
  纠正逻辑就会把错的当成对的。11-12 20:19 那次：日落 17:11，重启前后都是浅色，
  守护写「判定正确」就收工，整晚没变深色，只能手动重设。
- **现在**：每次从 `dumpsys uimode` 读 `sunrise` / `sunset`（拿不到按 19:00–07:00），
  算出「此刻应该深色还是浅色」，不再参考重启前的值。
- 重启后 45 秒、90 秒各查一次；之后每 10 分钟复查、持续 12 小时，
  日落/日出两个边界即使系统没生效也会在 10 分钟内被拉回。
- 你一旦自己改了模式（切成始终浅色/深色），守护立即退出，不跟用户抢。
- 新增 `NIGHT_STEP` / `NIGHT_SPAN` 两个环境变量可调节奏；`night` 子命令同样改为按 Twilight 判定。
- 读取 `dumpsys` 失败的轮次直接跳过，不会因为读不到状态而乱改模式。

releases.body:
## v2.1 —— 初始发布（versionCode 3）

首个公开版本。一个按钮让 KernelSU 模块生效，而不用拿折叠屏的副屏去换。

- 按 KernelSU 自己的流程执行 `post-fs-data` / `services` 两个阶段，然后只 `setprop ctl.restart zygote`，
  **不执行 `stop` / `start`**，SurfaceFlinger 全程存活，副屏（`port=148`）不掉
- `boot_completed` 看门狗：先扫描模块脚本里有没有 `resetprop -w` 等待者，有才在重启后制造一次
  0→1 边沿；没有就只保留「卡 0 太久 → 置 1」的安全网
- lspd 健康检查：三条硬指标（有 daemon、`lspbridge` 监听 ≥1、pid 不在旧快照）不满足就放弃重启
  zygote，避免「要点两次才生效」
- 夜间模式自愈：重启后若昼夜判定被改，先顶一个固定值再还原用户原本的模式；`trap` 保证任何
  退出路径（终端断开 / 进程被杀）都会还原
- 子命令：`check` 体检、`mods` 清单、`dump <id>` 打包、`trim` 清理重复实例、`night` 一条命令还原自动
- 日志落在 `/sdcard/GS/logs/`，不需要 root 就能读

作者：CodeFishK。实测环境：[GhostSam](https://github.com/snothin/GhostSam) 临时 root（三星 Z Fold7），
理论上任意 KernelSU / 兼容分支通用。

> 说明：v1.x、v2.0 是作者本机的内部迭代版本，从未对外发布，故不在此列出。
releases.name: v2.1 初始发布

Preserve inode source identity, retain active directory operations, prepare hooks before publishing children, bound unsigned UID cursors, and correct inode flags, dirents and legacy xattrs. releases.body:
- New: Game battery mode — off by default. Games get Android's battery mode with a 60 FPS cap and a lower render resolution, so they run cooler. On Android 13 the games to use are picked from the list; on Android 14+ every installed game is detected automatically.
- New: Pause charging / bypass charging — off by default. Charging pauses at the temperature or level you pick, or while a game is open, and the charger powers the phone instead. Kernels without a charging switch get bypass through a 0 mA charge current. Qualcomm and MediaTek.
- New: Battery history and temperature warning — off by default. A 48 h chart of level, temperature and screen-on / screen-off drain on Home, and a notification when the battery gets too hot.
- New: Leftover app folders — a new one-shot action finds Android/data and Android/obb folders of apps that are no longer installed, shows them and deletes them when you confirm.
- New: Memory bus frequency cap — off by default, Qualcomm. The RAM and system cache bus stays below its top speed for less heat under heavy load, with a lock so the ROM cannot raise it again.
- New: Lower screen resolution — off by default. The whole screen is drawn at 90, 80 or 75% with the same sizes on screen; the old values come back when it is turned off.
- Changed: C-state aware scheduler — Energy Aware Scheduler now also prefers cores that are awake or lightly asleep, on kernels that have the switch.
- Changed: Charge limit ~80% removed — the Xiaomi night charging limit and its keeper are gone. Use Pause / bypass charging instead; a limit set by an older version is released at the next boot.
- Changed: More charging-switch candidates: also Samsung (ac / dc charging_enabled, batt_slate_mode, stop_charge), Huawei (huawei_charger), Oplus (oplus_chg, google charger), Nubia (nubia_charge), LG (lge-unified-nodes), Transsion (CCIChargerSwitch, smb1357) and generic nodes; the battery keeper records a switch that leaves the battery Discharging as a cut and rejects it while gaming.

releases.body:
- New: Background app hibernation (off by default). User apps and preinstalled apps with launcher icons can be stopped a few minutes after the screen turns off, or closed manually from Home. Stop mode keeps apps asleep until opened; Close background processes only is the gentler option. Charging, protected, in-use, alarm-clock, default, and system-critical apps are skipped.
- New: `hibernate`, `hibernate_min`, and `hibernate_mode` settings in the WebUI, with hibernation results and skipped-app counts in Recent activity.
- New: System-background CPU tuning through `bg_sys_uclamp` and `bg_sys_latency`, reducing unnecessary scheduling work while allowing Android background tasks to share awake cores.
- New: TCP tuning through `x_net_tcp`, selecting the best available congestion control and configuring SACK, ECN, low latency, and timestamps. This option is now part of Faster network connections.
- Changed: HyperCool (Glacier) is available again as the original accent preset.
- Changed: Recent activity displays package labels and hibernation keeper status.
- Changed: The Home screen shows the last measured screen-off drain alongside the current estimate.
- Changed: The WebUI includes a What's New dialog for the current build.
- Changed: Routine screen-on keeper entries are no longer written to Recent activity.
- Fixed: Camera resolver packages such as `com.android.camera2` are excluded from hibernation to avoid stopping the camera on ROMs where the camera uses a resolver package.

releases.body:
- New: Wake sources report: kernel wakeup statistics in plain names (Mobile data, Wi-Fi, Apps and Android, Android system, Alarms and timers, Battery and charging, …), with how much of the time the phone was awake since "Mark start", sorting by awake time or wake-ups, and "Apps and Android" opening the apps that held wake locks. Read only.
- New: CPU use now: the busiest processes over 2 seconds as a share of the whole CPU, in plain names; the measurement itself and the root manager are left out, and reading `/proc` uses shell builtins only.
- New: Screen-off drain check (off by default): each screen-off period of 30 min or more without the charger is logged in Recent activity, with a notification when the drain is high (1 h or more, 2% or more lost, at the rate you pick) and the user app that held the most wake locks when the drain was 1%/h or more.
- New: `drain_alert`, `drain_alert_rate`, `drain_alert_notify`, `drain_cause` and `drain_cause_min` in the WebUI, read live by the keeper. App wake-lock rows and drain lines also get a "Block in background" button.
- Changed: `stats_reduce` now also turns off activity and foreground-service start logs and the disk stats logging job.
- Changed: the app wake-lock list reads `dumpsys batterystats --charged` (text, without the battery history), counts only per-uid partial wake locks, and gets package names from `cmd package list packages -U`.
- Changed: the screen-off drain check is off by default for new installs.
- Fixed: a charger plugged in during a screen-off period is detected from Android's `battery_status` events (with wake-up checks as a fallback), so those periods are left out even when `drain_cause` is off.
- Fixed: the drain check reads battery stats in the background with its own per-period mark (`wk.chk.<n>`), so a slow `dumpsys` never holds the keeper and a quick screen-off cannot clear its mark.
- Fixed: the module description reports "screen-off keeper running" when `drain_alert` is the only active keeper feature, and no drain line is logged when the drain check is off.

releases.body:
# KernelSU-Tailscaled v2.0.5

Fix standalone Android control-plane connectivity and update the official
Tailscale engine directly from the module WebUI.

## Android connectivity

- Bundle official Tailscale 1.104.2, including upstream standalone Android DNS,
  network monitoring, and CA support.
- Native Android mode selects the official interface-binding implementation
  (`TS_FORCE_LINUX_BIND_TO_DEVICE=true`). Control and UDP sockets no longer
  depend on an absent main-table default route for marked traffic. No copied
  default routes, hard-coded control hosts, or patched engine binaries.
- Restrict login DNS diagnostics to actual login states; ordinary startup is
  no longer treated as evidence of a fresh-login DNS failure.

## Update the engine from WebUI

Open **Tailscale engine update** in the module dashboard, check for an official
stable release, download and verify it, then explicitly apply it. Downloading
alone leaves the running service untouched. Applying briefly restarts the
module's service; it does not reboot Android or require signing in again.

- ARM and ARM64 downloads use the official HTTPS stable server and published
  SHA-256 checksum, with bounded downloads and restricted archive extraction.
- Activation preserves identity and configuration, validates service recovery,
  and restores the previous engine/state if activation fails.
- Interrupted transactions recover on the next lifecycle operation. A later
  stop or disable is respected; recovery does not silently override it.
- Separately updated engines survive module updates and boot; a newer bundled
  engine takes precedence. Downgrades are rejected by the normal updater.

## Validation

- Real Xiaomi test: temporarily ran 1.102.3, then checked, downloaded, verified,
  and applied 1.104.2 using the same controller actions as WebUI. The running
  executable changed to the downloaded engine; identity/configuration stayed
  unchanged, and public peer connectivity recovered. Normal runtime restored.
- OnePlus: updated engine retained across a module reinstall and authorized
  reboot, with automatic service activation.
- Automated coverage includes checksum/archive rejection, rollback, interrupted
  activation, disabled/stopped intent, and browser check/download/apply flow.
- See `docs/verification/2026-10-22-release-2.0.5.md` for evidence and limits.

The reporter's exact ROM and complete fresh-account browser authorization are
not yet verified. ARM32 packages are checked, but phone runtime testing is ARM64.

## Install

Install the universal or architecture-specific ZIP through KernelSU Manager.
Existing v2 identity and configuration are retained. Reopen Details after an
update to load the new WebUI. The withdrawn beta.1 is not a supported release.
releases.name: KernelSU-Tailscaled v2.0.5

## 4.0.5 (4.0.4 → 4.0.5)

### Highlights

- Added a KernelSU module package containing the supported KMI builds and userspace checker. It detects the device KMI, enables boot auto-load by default, and provides an Action button and multilingual WebUI for module controls and checker output.
- Added KernelSU Manager update metadata (`update.json`) and automated publication of versioned module assets, the checker, and the KernelSU ZIP. Release tags are checked against the module version; release creation accepts an HTTPS URL for release notes.
- Hardened controlled unload and hot-reload around live namespace and IPC state. The module tracks vendored namespace proxies, namespace-filesystem inode pins, IPC objects, and deferred cleanup; unsafe teardown is refused until references and work drain. Diagnostic resource counters help identify remaining blockers.
- Added procfs lookup fallbacks for `/proc/<pid>/ns/ipc` and `/proc/<pid>/ns/pid` when native namespace entries are unavailable, including an Android 17 / 6.18 path using that KMI's procfs PID accessor.

### Compatibility and testing

- The QEMU workflow exercises the checker before and after module load, namespace/procfs behavior, container workloads, and post-use module unload using pinned official Google GKI images across eight KMIs: `android12-5.10`, `android13-5.10`, `android13-5.15`, `android14-5.15`, `android14-6.1`, `android15-6.6`, `android16-6.12`, and `android17-6.18`.
- KernelSU ZIP and release packaging require a complete supported-KMI build matrix.
- `NET_NS` remains bookkeeping-only; use host networking (`--network=host`). The module must match the device's exact KMI. On Android data filesystems with casefold support, configure Docker to use `fuse-overlayfs` as described in the user guide.

### Changes

**fix:**
- Improved namespace/IPC lifetime handling, task-exit cleanup, and Android 5.10 compatibility; fixed KernelSU install permissions and shell invocation of control scripts.

**docs and licensing:**
- Added consolidated `copying.txt` terms to the project and KernelSU package, with clarified attribution and provenance metadata.

> This AI-generated release note is Public Domain.

releases.body:
# Magic V2Ray v4.0 Release Notes

### Highlights

- **Hotspot sharing without Shizuku**: share your proxy over hotspot using Wireless debugging (ADB) pairing and a built-in `app_process` helper.
- **Multi-hop proxy chains**: build chains of 2-16 hops.
- **In-app updates**: download, verify and install new APKs directly from the app.
- **External API level 2**: permission-gated node access for other apps.

### Added

- **ADB-based hotspot sharing (no Shizuku required)**
  - Wireless debugging pairing and an `app_process` helper, with ADB status and pairing controls in the Web UI and notification-based pairing.
  - Optional persistent ADB TCP mode that reconnects without re-pairing after the first wireless ADB connection. It can be disabled in settings, and a warning is shown that the port is reachable on networks the phone joins.
  - Configurable ADB TCP port: random or custom, persisted, validated from 1024 to 65535, and used for reconnections. The current port is shown on the pairing screen.
  - Localized setup, status and TCP-mode guidance.
- **Multi-hop proxy chains**
  - Create and configure chains with 2-16 hops, including dynamic hop selection and Xray outbound routing.
  - Duplicate nodes are allowed in a chain.
  - Legacy two-hop chain URIs are still supported.
  - Updated chain display, log export and plaintext checks for hop lists.
- **In-app APK update installation**
  - Downloads and verifies update APKs securely, then installs them through `PackageInstaller`.
  - Handles install permissions and shows progress in the Web UI.
  - Update info is now fetched without cache.
- **External API level 2**
  - Permission-gated node access: anonymous or full access, granted by user consent.
  - New provider methods for listing nodes and getting the active node, plus access management.
  - `connect` now supports direct, chained and node-ID URIs.
  - Added an English API guide documenting level 2 node access and special connect URIs.
- **Happy Eyeballs (RFC 8305)** for proxy and direct `freedom` outbounds, with interleaved address families and bounded concurrent connection attempts.
- **More ALPN and TLS fingerprint presets**: common choices added, custom ALPN values are preserved when editing, and MASQUE ALPN defaults to `h3`.
- **WebView navigation**: Android Back now dismisses the active modal and revisits previous tabs before sending the app to the background.

### Changed

- **Native HTTP bridge**: WebUI requests, downloads and probes no longer use shell-based `curl`. SOCKS routing is preserved, request limits and redirect schemes are enforced, and insecure TLS stays opt-in per subscription.
- **Native subscription updater**: the shell-based hourly updater is replaced by a stoppable native worker that downloads, decodes, caches and publishes changed subscriptions for the WebUI. Legacy updater processes are cleaned up, and host tests cover decoding, hashing and update behavior.
- **Geo-IP lookup** now queries `api.ip.sb` and `ipwho.is` in parallel, normalizes the responses, prefers the first complete result and keeps a valid partial result as a fallback.
- **MASQUE URI handling** synced with v2rayNG.
- **Documentation**: translated READMEs and API guides moved into locale directories. All README translations now explain that KernelSU ZIP downloads are installers, not APKs, and link to the Releases page for APK downloads.

### Fixed

- **Hotspot Binder handoff reliability**: the helper Binder is delivered through a synchronous `ContentProvider` call with broadcast fallbacks, and `adb shell` reads are bounded so detached helpers can no longer leave startup waiting indefinitely.
- **ROM-specific provider call signatures**: the correct `IContentProvider.call` overload is selected (preferring `AttributionSource`, falling back to the one with the most parameters) to avoid the deprecated Android 12 variant that forwards an invalid authority. The reflected method is logged, and plausible authority argument positions are tried.
- **Hotspot broadcasts** are now sent through `IActivityManager` first, with `Context` as a fallback, because bare `app_process` callers may lack an application thread and broadcasts could fail or be dropped.
- **Wireless debugging connections**: the TLS connect port is discovered through system properties and mDNS before falling back to library discovery. Early shell stream closure is tolerated, while replies indicating an unexpected shell UID are still rejected.
- **ADB pairing flow**: refreshed pairing screen and notifications with localized strings and status feedback. mDNS service resolution is serialized for Android versions that allow only one resolve request at a time.
- **System DNS leaks for local hosts**: reserved local names are excluded from system DNS queries, and dial probes resolve using configured or known local addresses, falling back to loopback.

### Notes

- Hotspot sharing via ADB requires Wireless debugging (Android 11+).
- KernelSU ZIP downloads are installers, not APKs. Download the APK from the repository Releases page.

---

[Click here for older release notes](https://github.com/vincentng295/Magic_V2Ray/releases)

- **Native HTTP bridge**: WebUI requests, downloads and probes no longer use shell-based `curl`. SOCKS routing is preserved, request limits and redirect schemes are enforced, and insecure TLS stays opt-in per subscription.
- **Native subscription updater**: the shell-based hourly updater is replaced by a stoppable native worker that downloads, decodes, caches and publishes changed subscriptions for the WebUI. Legacy updater processes are cleaned up, and host tests cover decoding, hashing and update behavior.
- **Geo-IP lookup** now queries `api.ip.sb` and `ipwho.is` in parallel, normalizes the responses, prefers the first complete result and keeps a valid partial result as a fallback.
- **MASQUE URI handling** synced with v2rayNG.
- **Documentation**: translated READMEs and API guides moved into locale directories. All README translations now explain that KernelSU ZIP downloads are installers, not APKs, and link to the Releases page for APK downloads.

### Fixed

- **Hotspot Binder handoff reliability**: the helper Binder is delivered through a synchronous `ContentProvider` call with broadcast fallbacks, and `adb shell` reads are bounded so detached helpers can no longer leave startup waiting indefinitely.
- **ROM-specific provider call signatures**: the correct `IContentProvider.call` overload is selected (preferring `AttributionSource`, falling back to the one with the most parameters) to avoid the deprecated Android 12 variant that forwards an invalid authority. The reflected method is logged, and plausible authority argument positions are tried.
- **Hotspot broadcasts** are now sent through `IActivityManager` first, with `Context` as a fallback, because bare `app_process` callers may lack an application thread and broadcasts could fail or be dropped.
- **Wireless debugging connections**: the TLS connect port is discovered through system properties and mDNS before falling back to library discovery. Early shell stream closure is tolerated, while replies indicating an unexpected shell UID are still rejected.
- **ADB pairing flow**: refreshed pairing screen and notifications with localized strings and status feedback. mDNS service resolution is serialized for Android versions that allow only one resolve request at a time.
- **System DNS leaks for local hosts**: reserved local names are excluded from system DNS queries, and dial probes resolve using configured or known local addresses, falling back to loopback.

### Notes

- Hotspot sharing via ADB requires Wireless debugging (Android 11+).
- KernelSU ZIP downloads are installers, not APKs. Download the APK from the repository Releases page.

---

- Updated the official NetBird client to v0.82.1 for x86_64, arm64-v8a, and armv7; release packaging verifies upstream SHA-256 checksums.

- Fixed userspace firewall handling of unspecified local addresses, prevented forwarded traffic from exiting its ingress interface, and corrected nftables peer-protocol matching behind IPv6 extension headers.

releases.body:
## v1.4.10 — NetBird v0.81.3
- Optimized the status watcher: one shared `status --json` call per cycle (was up to three netbird CLI spawns) with the module.prop description now parsed from JSON, and an idle mode while the client is disconnected — route re-checks and watchdog restarts are skipped and the cycle relaxes to `NB_IDLE_UPDATE_INTERVAL` (default 300s), so a downed client costs almost nothing. `webui up` starts a dead daemon on demand (detached, with auto-connect) and refreshes underlay routes immediately on reconnect.
- Added confirmed connection controls to the WebUI overview: Reconnect/Disconnect (fast daemon-IPC `up`/`down` reusing persisted flags) and Start/Stop daemon. Daemon lifecycle runs detached (`nohup`) with the page polling status, so closing the WebUI cannot interrupt it; every control requires a confirmation dialog. New fixed `webui` service actions: `up`, `down`, `daemon-start`, `daemon-stop`.
- Fixed the WebUI misreading a disconnected client as a stopped daemon: netbird's `daemonStatus` reports the connection state, so the page now tracks process state and connection state separately. After `webui down` the banner shows "disconnected" (with the stop/start controls intact) instead of switching to the start-daemon card; Connect/Disconnect buttons disable according to the current connection state and a needs-login state is surfaced.
- Restyled WebUI notices as centered translucent-gray toasts with rounded corners.
- Silenced the 5-second refresh cooldown on implicit loads (tab switches no longer pop an "updated recently" toast), deduplicated concurrent identical commands, and added a background Networks prefetch so the first Networks view renders instantly.
- Tab switches now render the destination view with its loading placeholder first and defer the data read until the slide transition finishes (240ms), removing the animation stutter caused by firing the root-command bridge mid-transition; stale timers are ignored when switching again quickly.
- Fixed the English "Refresh system routes"/"Refresh runtime rules" labels overflowing their two-column action buttons (shortened copy plus wrapping allowed in the action grid).
- Implicit-load failures now surface in-page instead of as toasts: Networks shows an error placeholder with retry, diagnostics show the error in the output area, and status-bridge errors appear as a detail line inside the banner. Toasts are reserved for explicit switch/confirm actions.
- When the daemon is stopped, views drop cached rows and show a "daemon is stopped" placeholder (Networks and Peers), and no doomed read commands are fired; the Networks cache is invalidated the moment status reports the daemon stopped, so stale rows never survive inside the 5-second cooldown.
- A running-but-disconnected client no longer triggers the raw "failed to list network: not connected" error: Networks shows a friendly not-connected placeholder (or a connecting indicator), the route rows and bulk enable/disable actions are hidden outside the healthy state, and the doomed `networks list` call is skipped; remaining error messages drop the CLI's "Error: " prefix.
- Fixed the watchdog restart path: `kill "$pid"2>/dev/null` was missing a space, so TERM/KILL targeted a nonexistent PID and a wedged daemon was never actually killed before the restart attempt.
- Deduplicated the busybox-timeout wrappers in the status watcher (`nb_with_timeout`) and made `client_cmd` delegate to `webui_client`.
- Removed the WebUI forwarding-rules view: NetBird dropped the `forwarding` CLI command in v0.81.0 together with management-side ingress ports, so the view always failed with `unknown command "forwarding"`.
- The `webui forwarding` service action now returns an explicit "no longer available in NetBird v0.81.0+" error instead of passing the raw CLI failure through, so stale cached WebUI pages show a clear message.
- The Networks view now shows a loading state while retrying after a failed load, matching the removed forwarding view's behavior.
- Moved the WebUI bridge sources (`view-model.mjs`, `kernelsu.js`) out of `module/webroot/` into `ui/src/`, so the shipped webroot contains only build output; removed the duplicate `ui/src/lib/utils.ts` and two unused i18n strings.
- Install-time extraction now skips the `update.json` / `updates/*.json` download manifests (managers fetch updates via the `updateJson` URL in `module.prop`, so the copies in `MODPATH` were dead weight).

## v1.4.9 — NetBird v0.81.3

- Updated the bundled official NetBird client from `0.80.0` to `0.81.3` for `x86_64`, `arm64-v8a`, and `armv7` packages, each archive SHA-256 verified against the official release checksums before packaging.
- Carries the upstream v0.81.x client changes: relayed connections in kernel mode no longer require eBPF (replaced by loopback endpoint addressing), one unreachable relay no longer churns the other relay connections, ICE session IDs survive remote restarts with fewer unnecessary reconnects, and the signal stream registration wait is bounded for faster failure detection.
- Re-created the `/dev/netbird` and `/dev/netbird.service` entry-point symlinks on every boot, so the CLI stays reachable after reboot on KernelSU without a mount metamodule (and in late-load mode), where `/dev` is wiped and the module's `system/bin` overlay is not mounted.
- On KernelSU, the dynamic module status is now also published through the `ksud module config` `override.description` key; Magisk and older managers keep reading the periodically refreshed `module.prop`.

## MirageForge v1.2.2

### 核心底层引擎升级
- **全新 COW Prop Spoof（写时复制私有属性覆写）**：在目标应用子进程内通过 `MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_FIXED` 将命中的系统属性区转为进程私有页并原地改写，完成后立即恢复 `r--p` 只读权限，绕过属性 PLT Hook 检测且对宿主机与其他应用保持 0 污染；与「伪装系统属性」建立三层强联动，关闭时自动同步释放。
- **6 大伪装能力细粒度拆分（严守 0 改动原则）**：拆分并独立控制 `伪装系统属性`、`COW Prop Spoof`、`伪装CPU`、`伪装GPU`、`伪装内存信息`、`伪装CPU/GPU文件节点`，未开启的子模块绝不挂载 Hook 或注入节点；老版本 `routes.db` 与 `config.json` 升级后自动无损迁移至 13 列格式。
- **Rust CLI 能力扩展**：
  - 新增 `device-info --json`，自动探测宿主设备型号、Android/内核版本、CPU 分簇、GPU 及当前活跃 Root 管理器（KernelSU / APatch / Magisk）与 Zygisk 实现（ReZygisk / Zygisk Next / NeoZygisk / Magisk Zygisk）。
  - 新增 `clone-device`，一键采集本机完整 `getprop`、每簇 `cpufreq` 频点表与内存/GPU 规格直接铸造模板。
  - 探针新增独立清空崩溃日志（`probe clear-crashes`）与一键导出排障诊断包（`probe bundle`）。

### 全新 4 主页界面与交互架构
- **重构为「首页 / 模板 / 应用 / 设置」4 主页体系**：支持方向性水平滑动切页，拆分模块化 Store 与样式体系。
- **首页**：新增顶部品牌宣传栏（含 OTA 更新提示条）、实时设备与 Root/Zygisk 环境信息卡片、模块生效统计卡片及探针/更新快捷入口。
- **模板**：顶部聚合 `在线模板`、`新建模板`、`导入/导出`（整合 `mf://` 分享口令、`build.prop` 属性炼金、一键克隆本机与备份导出）；模板卡片新增 **`生效应用`** 管理面板；编辑页升级为 **5 大分类宫格 + FLIP 几何全屏张开动画**（点击左上角 `←` 原路收缩返回），并内置硬件一致性体检。
- **应用**：改为带图标的整齐长条列表，每条下方直出当前伪装模板与活跃能力标签；点击进入独立全屏编辑页，顶部切换模板、下方提供 6 大**左侧独立开关**（灰=关 / 主题色=开）及折叠式屏幕高刷与高阶排障选项。
- **设置**：统一收口主题模式、5 套主题强调色、底栏形态（悬浮灵动栏 / 贴底常规栏）、液态玻璃质感、三语切换、MountNS / COW Prop 全局默认策略（支持一键同步至全部已配置应用）与诊断包导出。

### 真·光学四层液态玻璃与果冻物理引擎
- **四层光学折射架构**：基于 `userSpaceOnUse` 像素级 SDF 重写折射滤镜——`z:0` 底栏全域拉伸+柔焦、`z:1` 静止泡（压在图标下层，只拉伸柔和模糊背景而不扭曲图标）、`z:2` 锐利图标文字、`z:3` 交互水晶泡（0 模糊、仅外圈弧壁 Snell 弯曲拉伸），彻底消除偏移、发灰与明暗跳变。
- **体积守恒 Q 弹果冻物理引擎 (`JellySpring`)**：采用高精度子步进求解与独立果冻形变振荡器，支持按压回弹、拖动水滴拉伸、边界撞墙压扁与刹停余震；「仅毛玻璃」模式彻底独立隔离为纯净统一磨砂效果。

### 修复与适配
- 探针页新增独立「清空崩溃」按钮与顶部一键导出诊断包入口。

## MirageForge v1.2.2

### 核心底层引擎升级
- **全新 COW Prop Spoof（写时复制私有属性覆写）**：在目标应用子进程内通过 `MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_FIXED` 将命中的系统属性区转为进程私有页并原地改写，完成后立即恢复 `r--p` 只读权限，绕过属性 PLT Hook 检测且对宿主机与其他应用保持 0 污染；与「伪装系统属性」建立三层强联动，关闭时自动同步释放。
- **6 大伪装能力细粒度拆分（严守 0 改动原则）**：拆分并独立控制 `伪装系统属性`、`COW Prop Spoof`、`伪装CPU`、`伪装GPU`、`伪装内存信息`、`伪装CPU/GPU文件节点`，未开启的子模块绝不挂载 Hook 或注入节点；老版本 `routes.db` 与 `config.json` 升级后自动无损迁移至 13 列格式。
- **Rust CLI 能力扩展**：
  - 新增 `device-info --json`，自动探测宿主设备型号、Android/内核版本、CPU 分簇、GPU 及当前活跃 Root 管理器（KernelSU / APatch / Magisk）与 Zygisk 实现（ReZygisk / Zygisk Next / NeoZygisk / Magisk Zygisk）。
  - 新增 `clone-device`，一键采集本机完整 `getprop`、每簇 `cpufreq` 频点表与内存/GPU 规格直接铸造模板。
  - 探针新增独立清空崩溃日志（`probe clear-crashes`）与一键导出排障诊断包（`probe bundle`）。

### 全新 4 主页界面与交互架构
- **重构为「首页 / 模板 / 应用 / 设置」4 主页体系**：支持方向性水平滑动切页，拆分模块化 Store 与样式体系。
- **首页**：新增顶部品牌宣传栏（含 OTA 更新提示条）、实时设备与 Root/Zygisk 环境信息卡片、模块生效统计卡片及探针/更新快捷入口。
- **模板**：顶部聚合 `在线模板`、`新建模板`、`导入/导出`（整合 `mf://` 分享口令、`build.prop` 属性炼金、一键克隆本机与备份导出）；模板卡片新增 **`生效应用`** 管理面板；编辑页升级为 **5 大分类宫格 + FLIP 几何全屏张开动画**（点击左上角 `←` 原路收缩返回），并内置硬件一致性体检。
- **应用**：改为带图标的整齐长条列表，每条下方直出当前伪装模板与活跃能力标签；点击进入独立全屏编辑页，顶部切换模板、下方提供 6 大**左侧独立开关**（灰=关 / 主题色=开）及折叠式屏幕高刷与高阶排障选项。
- **设置**：统一收口主题模式、5 套主题强调色、底栏形态（悬浮灵动栏 / 贴底常规栏）、液态玻璃质感、三语切换、MountNS / COW Prop 全局默认策略（支持一键同步至全部已配置应用）与诊断包导出。

### 真·光学四层液态玻璃与果冻物理引擎
- **四层光学折射架构**：基于 `userSpaceOnUse` 像素级 SDF 重写折射滤镜——`z:0` 底栏全域拉伸+柔焦、`z:1` 静止泡（压在图标下层，只拉伸柔和模糊背景而不扭曲图标）、`z:2` 锐利图标文字、`z:3` 交互水晶泡（0 模糊、仅外圈弧壁 Snell 弯曲拉伸），彻底消除偏移、发灰与明暗跳变。
- **体积守恒 Q 弹果冻物理引擎 (`JellySpring`)**：采用高精度子步进求解与独立果冻形变振荡器，支持按压回弹、拖动水滴拉伸、边界撞墙压扁与刹停余震；「仅毛玻璃」模式彻底独立隔离为纯净统一磨砂效果。

### 修复与适配
- 探针页新增独立「清空崩溃」按钮与顶部一键导出诊断包入口。

## 版本 8.7.3（2026-11-25）

### 代理与策略组

- 服务停止时，代理页会标出 Selector 的默认节点，也可以直接换一个节点供下次启动使用。运行时切换节点会同步保存默认值，不重载服务。URLTest 仍由核心自动选择。
- 内核更新到 sing-box reF1nd 的 `reF1nd-testing-next` 快照（`77c0dbbe`），修复 Selector 将订阅节点设为默认值后冷启动失败的问题。若订阅更新后默认节点已不存在，但资源仍有效，核心会回退到可用成员。

### 入站与系统兼容

- 全新安装或选择「仅保留节点与订阅」时，默认使用 TUN 接管本机流量，不默认接管热点或 USB 网络共享。保留现有数据升级时，继续使用原有接管后端和设置。
- 新增 Google 联网兼容，适用于受支持的 ColorOS 16、红魔、努比亚和中兴固件。开机或模块热激活后自动检查，不依赖管理器或代理启动，不清空共享防火墙规则。

### 稳定性

- 修复配置事务恢复可能重新启动已明确停止的服务的问题；服务状态文件损坏时不再误报为正常停服。
- 完善诊断包的 TLS 私钥脱敏，并限制诊断归档大小。
- 同步 MIUIX Glass 0.9.5-beta04，优化模糊和弹层表现；减少策略组刷新与订阅更新中的重复工作。

### 升级说明

- 从 8.7.x 升级可选「保留现有数据」。建议使用模块包内附的管理器一并更新，本版不会用默认配置覆盖已保存的节点、策略组或路由。
- 从 8.6.2 或更早版本直升，请先备份并遵循 [8.7.0 的升级说明](https://github.com/Fanju6/NetProxy-Magisk/releases/tag/v8.7.0)。

## 版本 8.7.2（2026-11-22）

### 代理与策略组

- 默认配置只保留 `Proxy` 和 `Auto` 两个策略组。`Proxy` 默认选择 `Auto`，导入节点后可自动选择；没有节点时，需代理的流量仍会被拦截。原有内置分流的默认出口不变。
- 可在「代理 → 管理策略组 → 按订阅创建」为已有节点的订阅创建独立策略组。新增组不复制节点，也不会自动改动路由。
- 代理页直接显示原生标签；少量策略组均分标签栏，较多时仍可横向滚动。停服时直接显示已配置的成员，不再插入提示行。

### Android 管理器

- 修复冷启动或从其他页面切回仪表盘时误跳到代理页的问题。
- 手动测速结果会在退出并重进管理器后恢复显示；sing-box 重启后不会沿用旧结果。
- 同步 MIUIX Glass 0.9.5-beta03，适配顶栏折叠和搜索浮层行为。

### 升级说明

- 从 8.7.0 或 8.7.1 升级可选「保留现有数据」。已有策略组、默认成员和路由不会被新版默认配置替换；不必为使用新版而重置配置。
- 从 8.6.2 或更早版本直升，请先备份并遵循 [8.7.0 的升级说明](https://github.com/Fanju6/NetProxy-Magisk/releases/tag/v8.7.0)。

## 版本 8.7.1（2026-11-19）

### Android 管理器

- 管理器统一采用 MIUIX OS4 Glass，更新导航栏、菜单、弹层和应用图标。不支持实时折射的设备会在同一个安装包内回退。外观跟随系统明暗，仍可调整配色与界面缩放。
- 代理页的策略组标签可左右滚动，滑动仅浏览，点击才切换。新增、编辑、删除入口集中到右上角的「管理策略组」菜单；编辑时可调整兼容的组类型。
- 修复前后台切换时仪表盘服务卡片反复收起、代理节点选中标记闪烁的问题。回到前台重新确认核心状态前，不会发送可能作用于旧核心的节点切换。
- 应用代理改用右上角搜索入口。JSON 快捷工具栏可横向滚动，悬浮在代码上方并随键盘避让；日志页将常用操作收纳到菜单，清空前需确认。

### 路由与规则集

- 新建路由规则时可选择「指定策略组」，按域名、IP 或应用包名等条件选择出口。仍被路由引用的策略组不能直接删除；复杂规则继续用原生 JSON 编辑。
- 更新内置广告拦截规则、中国 IP 规则集和非中国地域规则集。

- 从 8.7.0 升级可选「保留现有数据」。从 8.6.2 或更早版本直升，请先备份并遵循 [8.7.0 的升级说明](https://github.com/Fanju6/NetProxy-Magisk/releases/tag/v8.7.0)。

## 版本 8.7.0（2026-11-12）

### 升级前必读

- **从 8.6.2 或更早的旧活动分组版本升级，请先备份，再选择「仅保留节点与订阅（配置恢复默认）」。** 新版不读取旧 `module.json` 的 `selection`，也不会补回旧版自动生成的出站。不要直接沿用整套旧配置。
- 此安装选项保留本地节点、订阅和模块日志，重置配置、本地规则及核心持久状态。升级后，请按需重新设置入站、应用代理和 Wi-Fi 策略；自定义 DNS、路由和出站请按新版结构逐项合回，不要直接覆盖新版主配置。
- 自定义策略组的 `providers` 现在引用资源名称，而非内部 ID。使用过旧 `np/<ID>` 引用的用户需要手动更新；已有重名或不符合命名规则的资源也需先改名。旧节点选择不会自动转到新策略组，启动后请重新选择节点或「自动选择」。

### 原生策略组

- 「代理」页现在展示 sing-box 原生策略组，支持展开列表和标签页布局、选择节点、测速，以及图形化创建或编辑 Selector 和 URLTest。
- 默认配置内置「自动选择」，并提供 AI、GitHub、YouTube、Google 等常用业务组。策略组和路由仍由同一份 sing-box 主配置管理。
- 服务停止时仍可浏览已保存的策略组成员；运行后以核心实际选择为准。仪表盘不再重复展示节点卡片。

### 资源管理

- 原「订阅」页改为「资源」，统一管理本地节点和 URL 订阅，保留节点图形化编辑、文本导入及订阅更新。
- 资源名称同时作为 Provider 标签，界面和原生配置使用同一名称。新建或改名遇到重名时自动追加序号，例如 `机场 (2)`。
- 精简资源详情摘要，修复离开代理页时选中标记提前消失的问题。

## 版本 8.6.2（2026-10-26）

### 内核与入站设置

- 内核更新至 `sing-box 1.15.0-alpha.13-reF1nd`，同步 Go 依赖及 JSON 编辑器补全与校验。
- 新安装的 eBPF 本机与共享网络数据平面默认使用 `socket_assign`；共享网络仍默认关闭。
- 入站设置新增独立的数据平面选择：本机支持 `socket_assign` 与兼容模式 `cgroup`，共享网络支持 `socket_assign` 与兼容模式 `packet_rewrite`，两者可以不同。
- 高级设置新增“允许共享接口作为默认上游”，默认关闭，用于按需配置单接口网关。
- eBPF 能力预检同步所选数据平面、cgroup 路径与 FakeIP ICMP 设置；非默认 UDP 会话超时不得短于 5 秒。

### 升级说明

- 保留现有数据升级不会强制改写已有的 `cgroup` 或 `packet_rewrite` 选择；省略数据平面时使用模块默认的 `socket_assign`。
- 旧本机 `local.data_plane: "tc"` 已移除，使用自定义入站 JSON 的用户需手动改为 `socket_assign`，不提供自动转换。
- `socket_assign` 需要相应的 BPF、网络命名空间、veth 和系统权限支持；不支持时会明确报错，不自动回退，可手动选择对应兼容模式。

## 版本 8.6.0（2026-10-15）

### 管理器连接

- Android 管理器全面改用模块 HTTPS 管理接口，不再申请 Root 权限或通过 Root Shell 执行命令；模块仍需 Root 环境。
- 管理器自动获取可信连接资料，无需手动复制密钥；使用独立的安装证书和随机凭据保护本机管理接口。
- 服务状态、流量、节点与订阅通过共享事件连接更新，切换页面时复用连接。

### 模块管理接口

- 新增独立于 sing-box 的 HTTPS API，支持节点、订阅、配置、日志与服务管理；核心停止时仍可访问。
- HTTP API 与 CLI 共用业务校验和配置事务；已接受的写入不因客户端断开而中断，保存失败与运行时同步失败分别反馈。
- 接口监听失败后自动退避恢复，无需重启代理核心。

### 应用与节点

- 应用标签、图标与多用户信息由模块统一提供，图标按需读取并复用缓存，刷新时保留已显示的图标。
- 没有节点的分组不再显示 Auto-Fastest 卡片。

## 版本 8.7.3（2026-11-25）

### 代理与策略组

- 服务停止时，代理页会标出 Selector 的默认节点，也可以直接换一个节点供下次启动使用。运行时切换节点会同步保存默认值，不重载服务。URLTest 仍由核心自动选择。
- 内核更新到 sing-box reF1nd 的 `reF1nd-testing-next` 快照（`77c0dbbe`），修复 Selector 将订阅节点设为默认值后冷启动失败的问题。若订阅更新后默认节点已不存在，但资源仍有效，核心会回退到可用成员。

### 入站与系统兼容

- 全新安装或选择「仅保留节点与订阅」时，默认使用 TUN 接管本机流量，不默认接管热点或 USB 网络共享。保留现有数据升级时，继续使用原有接管后端和设置。
- 新增 Google 联网兼容，适用于受支持的 ColorOS 16、红魔、努比亚和中兴固件。开机或模块热激活后自动检查，不依赖管理器或代理启动，不清空共享防火墙规则。

### 稳定性

- 修复配置事务恢复可能重新启动已明确停止的服务的问题；服务状态文件损坏时不再误报为正常停服。
- 完善诊断包的 TLS 私钥脱敏，并限制诊断归档大小。
- 同步 MIUIX Glass 0.9.5-beta04，优化模糊和弹层表现；减少策略组刷新与订阅更新中的重复工作。

### 升级说明

- 从 8.7.x 升级可选「保留现有数据」。建议使用模块包内附的管理器一并更新，本版不会用默认配置覆盖已保存的节点、策略组或路由。
- 从 8.6.2 或更早版本直升，请先备份并遵循 [8.7.0 的升级说明](https://github.com/Fanju6/NetProxy-Magisk/releases/tag/v8.7.0)。

releases.body:
## NoMount v2.3.1 is here! 🎉

This release is all about making the metamodule as fast and as self-contained as possible. The heavy lifting that used to happen in shell (`find`, one `sh` per batch, `xargs`, `rule-paths.sh`) now lives inside `nm`. Module load, unload and listing are a single native pass, whiteouts / opaque dirs / `.replace` / `.remove` are resolved by the binary, and the WebUI reads everything through that same listing. The module list is now up to 100x faster and boot injection no longer spawns a shell per file.

The kernel also got another hot-path and lifetime pass. The wire protocol is still v23, so there are no ABI changes: the new module works with the 2.3.0 driver and vice versa. Still, there are enough kernel fixes here that you should update both together.

### Small Changelog:
> There are too many changes in this version, so this is sort of a summary of most important changes of this release :)

- kernel/:
  - Rule path hashes are computed once and reused, and the synthetic virtual-parent rule is now shared instead of allocated and copied per operation. This adds up during boot with thousands of rules.
  - Revalidation reuses the directory leaf already bound to the inode instead of probing the hash table again, and `nm_child_matches` short-circuits empty names.
  - Rule validation on add: empty names, `NAME_MAX` overflows, unknown flags, conflicting whiteout/opaque/virtual-dir flags and malformed UID ranges are rejected; trailing slashes are normalized.
  - `.` and `..` path components are rejected and dot entries are skipped in readdir, so a rule can no longer be created for a name that the actor can never match.
  - A rule whose backing path resolves to a virtual inode is rejected (#120), preventing loops. Rename targets and hardlinks on virtual inodes are rejected with `-EPERM`.
  - Invalid backing child dentries are dropped during revalidation, so a replaced or removed backing file no longer keeps serving a stale dentry.
  - Virtual inode size is synced from the backing inode on open and write, so `stat`/`fstat` reports the real size after writes.
  - Async direct I/O on virtual files is rejected with `-EOPNOTSUPP`, since the proxy don't handle it.
  - Repeated mmaps no longer dirty the virtual inode `S_PRIVATE` flag (atomic clear), removing a cacheline write from the mmap hot path.
  - Virtual directory entries now emit their real `d_type` (char, block, fifo, socket, symlink, ...), not just dir/reg, so `ls`, `find` and other readdir consumers see the right type.
  - File handles now preserve the native `encode_fh` for real inodes, and refuse to encode virtual inodes (`-ESTALE`) instead of handing them to NFS/FUSE/overlay export paths (thanks @1385721 to report this bug).
  - Superblock hooks are removed on `put_super` before the superblock can be freed, hook/unhook is unified, and fake xattr tables are freed after an RCU grace period. Fixes a class of UAFs on unmount.
  - Hijacked callbacks fall back to the live `i_op`/`f_op` when the original pointer is being restored, closing a race during rule teardown.
  - Leaf hash table grew from 64 to 1024 buckets, and the UID exclusion bloom filter from 256 to 1024 bits. Rule control lookups and `nomount_is_uid_blocked` collide far less on devices with many rules
  - `setup.sh` without arguments now actually follows the newest `v*` tag (fetching tags first) instead of blindly pulling `dev`; an explicit tag or commit still works.
  - `Kconfig` now `select`s `KEYS`. NoMount genuinely needs the keyring, and kernels built with `CONFIG_KEYS=n` no longer fail to compile.

- userspace/:
  - **New `nm module load <mod_path> [--targets=...]` and `nm module unload <mod_path>`.** The whole module tree is walked in C, in one pass, replacing the old `find | sh rule-paths.sh | xargs` pipeline.
    - All partitions are auto-detected (`system`, `system_ext`, `vendor`, `odm`, `product`, `apex`, `my_*`, ...), with `--targets` to override the list.
    - `.replace` with content becomes an opaque rule, `.replace` alone or empty becomes a whiteout, `.remove` becomes a whiteout, character devices become whiteouts, and symlinks are resolved with loop detection.
    - `trusted.overlay.opaque=y` is honored, and a failed xattr probe simply degrades to "not opaque" instead of aborting the module.
    - Whiteouted directories skip their whole subtree on load, while unload still walks them to remove every rule underneath.
    - Reports `nm_load_status` / `nm_unload_status` on stderr so the boot scripts and the WebUI can react.
  - **New `nm module list --json [--only=a,b]`.** Lists `/data/adb/modules` natively, reads the real name from `module.prop`, the `disable` and `skip_mount` markers, and counts the live rules per module (whiteouts are attributed by virtual path). This is what makes the WebUI listing fast and correct.
  - Rule batching was reworked into a single bounded pass, flushing pages as they fill. Per-rule errors no longer abort the rest of the batch, and invalid paths/UIDs are reported with an explicit message.
  - UID and range parsing is overflow-safe and validated; paths are normalized (`//`, `.`/`..`, trailing slashes) before they reach the driver.
  - `nm --try-lock` internal mode lets the module scripts take a `flock` through the binary, with no dependency on the `flock` utility.

- module/:
  - **Boot injection is now one `nm module load "$mod_path"` per module.** `rule-paths.sh` and `dump_rules.sh` are gone, along with the `find`/`xargs`/per-file shell forks. Whiteouts, opaque dirs, `.replace`/`.remove` and char devices are all handled by the binary.
  - **Locks were reworked:** each stage takes a dedicated `.boot.flock` / `.lkm.flock` / `.inject.flock` through `nm --try-lock` (no `flock` binary), and the injection lock is held until the script exits. A killed stage can't leave a stale lock behind because the kernel releases the fd, and `metamount.sh` now aborts cleanly on `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`.
  - The installer prefers `ksud insmod` / `apd insmod` when the root manager supports it, falling back to `lkmloader`, with clearer error messages.
  - `service.sh` logs failures when applying excluded UIDs and the isolated-UID flag instead of swallowing them.
  - `boot-completed.sh` only clears the boot semaphore; the lock files are managed by the flock implementation.

- webui/:
  - **Module listing is a single `nm module list --json` call.** No shell loop, no `find`, no per-file `sh`, no JSON stitching in JS: module cards, file counts, whiteout/opaque attribution and statuses all come from one native listing. It is up to 100x faster and stays correct with `.replace`/`.remove`, whiteouts and opaque dirs.
  - Loading and unloading a module from the WebUI is a single `nm module load` / `nm module unload` call, using the exact same walk as boot.
  - **UI state is read with a single shell command:** UID list, exclusions, safe mode, dump-rules flag and isolated-UID state arrive in one `exec` separated by a marker, instead of one `exec` per value. This makes the webui open more fast.
  - The app list is cached in `localStorage` with a 5-minute TTL and refreshed in the background. The first paint uses the cache, `pm list packages` runs in parallel for multiple users, and the selector re-renders in place when the refresh lands.
  - Home stats and module cards are updated from the cached listing; toggling a module no longer re-lists every module.
  - **Rule-to-module attribution moved into the binary.** The old JS walk over rules, modules and path parents is gone, so listing cost no longer explodes with the number of rules.
  - Material You seed detection was fixed: it reads the live `--primary`, falls back to `cmd overlay lookup` accent tones, and caches the seed, so theme colors are stable and correct.
  - Module ids and paths passed to the shell are quoted, closing an injection/whitespace bug.
  - Removed redundant work from the render paths (cached `scrollTop`, no duplicate lookups), and a missing home cache no longer logs an error.

and a lot of other misc changes :)

#### Thanks to everyone who kept testing, contributing and reporting through this one: @ZQZCC, @sohan-f, and the testers on the Telegram group 🫂

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/maxsteeel/nomount/compare/v2.3.0-720...v2.3.1

releases.body:
## NoMount v2.2.0 is here!🎉

This release brings UID-scoped rules, opaque directory redirection, `.remove` support, and the biggest hot-path optimization pass we've ever shipped. The kernel driver and the metamodule **must be updated together**.

> Commit count hit 605 on this release. Driver protocol is now v22. Thanks to everyone who kept reporting, bisecting and testing through the rough week 💙

### Small Changelog:

- kernel/:
  - Wire protocol v22. `nm_rule_hdr` grew from 16 to 24 bytes and `nm_del_hdr` from 10 to 18 to fit the new UID range fields. A v22 CLI cannot talk to a v21 driver (and vice versa); the installer aborts if the running driver is older than v22.
  - UID-scoped rules with ranges: `--uid-range 1000-5000` and `--uid-range all`. A single rule now covers a whole range without enumerating every UID.
  - UID deny sub-ranges: `--uid-excluded 3000-4000`. Combine it with `--uid-range` for `[1000,5000] except [3000,4000]`, or use it alone as "default except this range". Rules with the same target range but different denies are rejected with `-EEXIST`; overlap between ranges is rejected too.
  - Opaque directories: `--opaque`. A directory rule can hide the underlying filesystem entirely and only expose the module's leaves. This is what `.replace` with content actually meant: previously it whiteouted the whole directory and bootlooped when the hidden dir was a system app the framework needed.
  - Pseudo filesystems (`proc`, `sysfs`, `devpts`, `debugfs`, `tracefs`, `selinuxfs`, `cgroup`, `bpf`) are no longer hijacked at the dentry level.
  - Skip d_op installation on dentries that have no rule for their name. This is the biggest change in the release: it removes the d_revalidate tax on every non-rule lookup under a hijacked directory, which is most of them.
  - Skip d_op installation on dentries in pseudo filesystems, and skip the `shrink_dcache_parent` pass when invalidating a single injected name. The `nm_hijack_dentry_ops` publication now uses `smp_store_release` and a single `d_flags` write.
  - Hot-path micro-optimizations, reorder `nm_dir_ops` so the hot fields fit in one cache line, avoid `current_fsuid()` when the leaf is NULL, skip `nm_is_uid_blocked()` and `nm_find_leaf_in_dir()` when there is no leaf or no children, short-circuit `nm_dir_lookup` and `nm_d_revalidate_common` on directories without rules.
  - `nm_d_revalidate_common` no longer reads `dentry->d_op` or `inode->i_op` when it does not need them, and chains to the original `d_revalidate` when the underlying filesystem has one.
  - On unload, walk `i_dentry` to clear `d_op` before freeing module memory. Fixes the panic on `rmmod` with files open on virtual paths.
  - `iget5_locked` hits no longer allocate an `nm_inode_info`; the probe uses a stack struct and `kmalloc` only happens for `I_NEW`. `d_add` instead of `d_splice_alias` for fresh file inodes.
  - Probe `xattr_handler->__get` via header grep instead of `LINUX_VERSION_CODE`, so kernel trees that never backported the member compile again.
  - `inode_state_read_once` for I_NEW checks (mainline >=6.19 compatibility).
  - Deferred reclaim of rules and leaves moved fully to process context. `nm clear rules` no longer blocks on `synchronize_rcu`.
  - Internal naming unified to the `nm_` prefix.

- userspace/:
  - `--uid-range <a>-<b>`, `--uid-range all`, `--uid-excluded <c>-<d>`, and `--opaque` flags.
  - `nm rule list` prints `[UID: a-b excl c-d]` and emits `"opaque": true` in the JSON output.
  - Streamlined absolute path handling, chunked output for large rule lists.

- module/:
  - `common.sh` holds the boot pipeline: bootloop detection keyed on `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`, LKM loading, module disable. `post-fs-data.sh` and `metamount.sh` are thin wrappers over it.
  - Boot order is now correct on both KernelSU and APatch. The previous flow silently lost rules on APatch (and sometimes in KernelSU with specific setups) because metamount.sh ran before the LKM was loaded.
  - Bootloop detection no longer relies on `.booting` existence; a successful boot clears the file, a failed boot keeps the boot_id and the next boot disables the module.
   - `.remove` support: Magisk's .remove marker is recognized alongside `.replace` (`.replace` with content → opaque rule, `.replace` alone → whiteout, `.remove` → whiteout).  `rule-paths.sh` gains `path`, `pair`, `opaque` and `del` kinds, and both `metamount.sh` and the WebUI's hot load/unload use the same flow. Hot unload now deletes opaque rules too.
  - `x86_64` build support: new CI matrix entry, `lkmloader-x86_64`, `nm-x86_64`, and `ARCH_BIN` normalization for KernelSU's `x64` label.
  - Installer aborts if the running driver is below v22, and falls back to the previous LKM if a v22 KO is staged for the next boot. Reboot is required to activate the new driver in LKM mode.

- webui/:
  - Skip / Unskip button on each module card (creates or deletes `skip_mount`).
  - Persist the "Show system apps" toggle across reloads.
  - Back gesture closes the right dialog in every navigation state (fixed double back navigation).
  - AMOLED palette adjustments and clear button corner fix.

and a lot of other misc changes :)

#### Thanks to everyone who kept testing, contributing and reporting through the rough bits: @ZQZCC, @nleloc, @sohan-f, and the testers on the Telegram group 🫂

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/maxsteeel/nomount/compare/v2.1.1...v2.2.0

  - `service.sh` logs failures when applying excluded UIDs and the isolated-UID flag instead of swallowing them.
  - `boot-completed.sh` only clears the boot semaphore; the lock files are managed by the flock implementation.

- webui/:
  - **Module listing is a single `nm module list --json` call.** No shell loop, no `find`, no per-file `sh`, no JSON stitching in JS: module cards, file counts, whiteout/opaque attribution and statuses all come from one native listing. It is up to 100x faster and stays correct with `.replace`/`.remove`, whiteouts and opaque dirs.
  - Loading and unloading a module from the WebUI is a single `nm module load` / `nm module unload` call, using the exact same walk as boot.
  - **UI state is read with a single shell command:** UID list, exclusions, safe mode, dump-rules flag and isolated-UID state arrive in one `exec` separated by a marker, instead of one `exec` per value. This makes the webui open more fast.
  - The app list is cached in `localStorage` with a 5-minute TTL and refreshed in the background. The first paint uses the cache, `pm list packages` runs in parallel for multiple users, and the selector re-renders in place when the refresh lands.
  - Home stats and module cards are updated from the cached listing; toggling a module no longer re-lists every module.
  - **Rule-to-module attribution moved into the binary.** The old JS walk over rules, modules and path parents is gone, so listing cost no longer explodes with the number of rules.
  - Material You seed detection was fixed: it reads the live `--primary`, falls back to `cmd overlay lookup` accent tones, and caches the seed, so theme colors are stable and correct.
  - Module ids and paths passed to the shell are quoted, closing an injection/whitespace bug.
  - Removed redundant work from the render paths (cached `scrollTop`, no duplicate lookups), and a missing home cache no longer logs an error.

and a lot of other misc changes :)

#### Thanks to everyone who kept testing, contributing and reporting through this one: @ZQZCC, @sohan-f, and the testers on the Telegram group 🫂

## What's changed

This release migrates OMK and the injector from `rsbinder` to Android's native Binder runtime. Binder objects, Parcels, and private Unix-socket RPC now use the device's Binder libraries, with shared interfaces generated by the official Android SDK Rust AIDL backend. Android 13 or above is now required.

Keystore interception now runs through native Binder callbacks and generated AIDL dispatchers. The ioctl hook redirects validated local receivers and tracks transaction lifetimes, replacing the previous manual Parcel parsing, reply rewriting, and operation-publication machinery. Caller UID, PID, and SELinux identity, transaction flags, interface metadata, and one-way calls follow the native dispatch path, with version-specific handling for older framework layouts and KeyMint parameter decoding.

Live security-level handles now follow the current caller filter and per-method intercept settings, returning to System when interception is disabled or the caller is no longer selected. Existing OMK operations remain bound to the RPC session that created them. RPC connection recovery now runs in the background and publishes the main, auth-token, and lifecycle connections together. Ordinary requests remain on System while connections are unavailable or confirmed stale, and OMK routing resumes after recovery. Calls already dispatched to OMK preserve its business errors and actual Binder failures without synthetic middleware error codes.

Authentication tokens now retain their original System MAC when received and cached. Before an OMK operation uses a token, System KeyMint verifies the MAC and OMK translates it for its own KeyMint. Successful translation is cached per operation for subsequent AAD, update, and finish calls, and translation failures trigger operation cleanup. The existing `force_skip_system_biometric_hat_verification` switch remains the explicit MAC-verification bypass.

System HAT verification now supports KeyMint devices exposed through `android.security.compat`, explicitly requests SHA-256 for HMAC verifier operations, and preserves authentication failures instead of collapsing them into a generic system error. Cached verifier keys are regenerated only when invalid or requiring an upgrade.

Payload fd handoff and remote-call cleanup were tightened, dependencies were updated, and builds now require Android SDK Build Tools 37.0.0 for AIDL generation.
